Subject: Post-demo: log sanitization approach & SLA checklist

Hi Sam / Alice —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time and for walking through the integration surface. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the logging/sanitization items you asked about during the demo: 

1) What we capture: by default Redwood logs request/response metadata (timestamps, model id, route, token counts) and the full request/response payloads only when customers opt-in. We recommend enabling request payload logging in staging for initial debugging, then turning on prefix/KV caching to reduce payload retention.

2) Redaction strategy: we provide configurable header redaction and field-level masking. For trace identifiers and any header values you mark as sensitive we can either:
  - redact (replace with constant [REDACTED]), or
  - pseudonymize (stable hash with rotation policy) — useful if you need joinability without exposing raw IDs.

3) Retention & residency: logs can be retained for configurable windows (7/30/90/365 days). For MedCure we can keep logs in US-only regions and support an on-prem delivery bundle for audit extracts.

4) SLAs & controls: dedicated customers can get contract language for data retention, deletion windows, and evidence (audit logs + metrics). SOC 2 artifacts are available; we can include a tailored appendix about logging controls.

Attachments: medcure-redaction-specs.pdf (draft mapping from demo) and a diagram (redwood-pseudonymization-diagram.png).

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll share the redaction spec (attached) and a short checklist mapping each MedCure requirement to our config knobs by EOD tomorrow.
- If you want, we can schedule a 30-min working session with engineering to go line-by-line on the fields you want masked/pseudonymized.

If that all looks right, tell me your preferred time window for a working session and whether you prefer redact vs pseudonymize for trace IDs initially.

Thanks,

Priyom — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions from the security team: 

- For trace identifiers: we need to ensure they are never stored in plaintext in long-term logs. We prefer pseudonymization with rotation and the ability to re-resolve only under approved legal process. Is that supported?
- Header coverage: during some of our calls we saw that trace IDs appear in both request headers and internal X-Forwarded fields. Can you confirm Redwood's config lets us list header names to sanitize (including wildcard patterns)?
- Developer access: will developer service accounts have access to full request bodies in staging by default? We want to avoid accidental exposure.

Also: Can you share the expected timeline to enable redaction in a Dedicated environment vs Hosted? We have an internal gating decision next week.

Thanks,

Sam — really appreciate the specificity. Short answers first, then proposed follow-up items: 

- Pseudonymization & rotation: yes. We can issue a stable, salted HMAC for trace IDs with a rotation cadence you choose (30/90/365 days). Re-resolution (to the original value) is supported only for customers on Dedicated or Private with a legal/ops process; for Hosted customers we do not store the salt in reversible form.

- Header pattern rules: supported. You can supply explicit header names or simple glob patterns (e.g., "X-Trace-*"), and the runtime will apply the redaction/pseudonymization pipeline before any logs are persisted.

- Developer access: by default, staging accounts in Hosted do not get persistent full-body access — there's a feature flag and an audit gate. For Dedicated we can scope SRE/dev role permissions and remove body-level access entirely for non-admins.

Timeline: enabling configuration in a Dedicated environment is typically a 2-week ops onboarding (policy + config deployment) once contracts are signed. Hosted changes (per-customer header rules) can be applied in 1-3 business days for non-invasive rules; deep retention policy changes may need a technical review.

Deliverables I will attach once you confirm:
- A one-page redaction checklist mapped to your demo notes
- Example header glob file you can drop into your config
- SOC 2 evidence packet and a short write-up of our rotation policy

Would Wednesday 10/28 09:00 PT work for a 30-min working session with our infra engineer (Ben)?

Best,
